as_told.title: SRI remote viewing tests and Ingo Swann

plain: The CIA is said to have run a psychic spy program, led by a physicist named Hal Puthoff, in which "remote viewers" claimed to describe faraway places with their minds alone, and some of them reported seeing beings. Michels tells this himself. He says remote viewers saw beings in various places, including, in the case of a viewer named Ingo Swann, "the Dark Side of the Moon." The writer Peter Levenda stresses something else: the test results. He tells Michels that the tests at SRI, the California research institute where the work was done, showed "statistical improvements", and that Swann "did tremendous work." If true, it would mean the government studied psychic abilities seriously and found that they worked.
